$about: Single source of truth for dylan.blog's visual identity. Consumed by scripts/generate-instagram.js and scripts/build-brand-book.js. Edit this file, never docs/BRAND-BOOK.md.

identity.name: dylan.blog
identity.premise: A point-and-click adventure game that happens to be a 23-year-old personal blog.

type.$note: Type is intentionally per-mode: each mode has its own typographic personality. Fantasy is the base and supplies the fallbacks.

rendering.$note: All sprite and header art must render with image-rendering: pixelated. Smoothing a pixel sprite is the one unforgivable sin.

fantasy.note: Not a theme class — it IS the default, defined in style.css. Every other mode overrides it.

underwater.note: Stacks its background over fantasy's as a fallback layer — the only mode that does.

corporate.note: The only mode built on CSS custom properties, and they live in style.css rather than themes.css. The pattern every other mode should have followed.

western.note: Barely exists: 12 art files total across eight directories (one background, one header, five sprites) and two CSS rules. A placeholder skeleton, not a theme.

kaiju.note: Further along than western — 42 art files including 19 real category headers — but zero category sprites and still only two CSS rules. The closest of the two to being finishable.

tech.use: Programming, gadgets, blog updates, coding projects

health.use: Medical, chronic illness, recovery, healthcare system rants

reading.use: Book reviews, recommendations, the Magpie's Library book club

tabletop.use: Blood Bowl, Warhammer, D&D, board games, miniatures

crafting.use: Puppets, sewing, bow ties, making things

clowning.use: Performance, circus arts, juggling, balloons, magic

adhd.use: ADHD and mental health, framed as lived experience

genreThemes.$note: A review card is skinned by the book's genre, using the site's own modes. Only modes that own a reading header AND a reading category sprite can carry a card; the rest fall back to fantasy. This is what finally gives the modes a job beyond a novelty toggle.

unavailable.kaiju: Has a reading header but no category sprite. Draw one and horror/monster books can use it.
unavailable.western: No reading art at all. Needs a header and a sprite before westerns can be skinned.
unavailable.corporate: Two headers total, no reading art. Business and nonfiction have nowhere to go yet.

orphanedArt.$note: Art that exists on disk but has no category. Kept so nobody 'rediscovers' it and wires it up by accident.
orphanedArt.garden.png: Header art, zero posts have ever used a garden category.
orphanedArt.ornate frome.png: Misfiled in headers/ and misspelled — it is a frame, not a category header.

story.use: Story frames; link stickers are added in the app, never baked in

reviewCard.$note: Furniture specific to book reviews. The prose format is two depths — shelf talker (250-400 words) and full review (800-1200) — sharing this card.

animation.name: barber
animation.note: Blog embed only. The Instagram PNG freezes a frame.

enjoymentBar.numberNote: The bar never shows a number, anywhere. On a book card a percentage reads as reading progress — Kindle, StoryGraph and Goodreads all use it that way. A number also reintroduces the "is it 70 or 75" dithering the bar exists to avoid.

shelfTags.$note: Breadth, not quality. Orthogonal to the enjoyment bar, so the two can never contradict each other.
shelfTags.hand-sell: I will put this in your hands
shelfTags.right-reader: Niche, but if it is you, it is YOU
